findings.title: Include identity type in the denial-cache key
findings.body: The denial key uses only the parsed subject ID and omits IdentityType, even though permissions differ by identity type. For example, a denied dashboards:read check for anonymous:0 caches a denial that also matches render:0 for the same namespace, dashboard and folder. The renderer is explicitly granted wildcard read permission, but the early cache return now denies it without evaluating those permissions for 30 seconds. Include the identity type (or full subject) in the key to isolate these identities.

findings.title: Encode denial-cache components without ambiguous separators
findings.body: Concatenating resource name and parent folder with underscores produces collisions when either identifier contains underscores. For the same namespace, user and action, name=a_b with parent=c produces the same key as name=a with parent=b_c. A denial for one resource therefore incorrectly denies access to the other, even if its permissions allow access, because Check returns immediately on a denial-cache hit. Use an unambiguous encoding of the components, such as a serialized tuple or length-prefixed values.
